subject: VM technical addendum and pen-test/SBOM deliverables for Everluma
messages:
From: Jordan Llewellyn <security@everluma.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@everluma.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on pen test output, SBOM provenance, and patch SLAs

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we assemble the security pack for our procurement review, we need some clarifications so the information can flow to our risk committee:

1) Pen-test summary: can you confirm the scope (external infra vs. application layer) and whether mitigations were validated by re-test or design changes? We need a one-page summary with CVSS distribution and any critical/high findings that remain open.

2) SBOM provenance: we require a snapshot of the SBOM used for the build you referenced (June 2027). Please include tool/format (e.g., SPDX), the commit/tag used, and whether third‑party scanning was applied.

3) Patch SLAs and exception policy: our procurement requires defined SLAs for critical/high/medium findings and a policy for emergency patches. Please state typical SLA windows and any SOC or change-management constraints.

4) SAST/DAST coverage: which tools do you run (internal or third‑party), cadence (pre-release, CI gate, periodic), and retention of findings.

We'd like these items as an addendum to the RFP packet by EOD Thursday (2027-07-15). If some items are sensitive, indicate redaction options and evidence we can accept (e.g., pen-test executive summary + attestation).

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Llewellyn
Head of Security, Everluma
security@everluma.com

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Jordan Llewellyn <security@everluma.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, procurement@everluma.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifications on pen test output, SBOM provenance, and patch SLAs

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. We prepared an addendum and attached the artefacts you requested (see attached PDF / ZIP). High level answers below; attached pack has concise artifacts and a redacted pen-test exec summary suited for vendor distribution.

1) Pen-test summary
- Scope: external network + authenticated web application layer and API endpoints (OWASP Top 10 + custom auth checks). No internal host-only testing without customer approval.
- Validation: remediation verification is performed where fixes are deployed to a staging environment. For the June 2027 engagement, 18 of 22 findings were verified after remediation; the remaining 4 were design-level recommendations (low/med). See pen_test_summary_202706.pdf for CVSS table and verification status.

2) SBOM provenance
- Format: SPDX v2.2 (JSON), produced at build tag: release/2027-06-14 (commit: b3f2c9a).
- Tooling: internal build pipeline exports SBOM; we run third-party composition scanning (OSS-Guard v3.1) as part of CI. The sbom_snapshot_202706.zip includes the SPDX JSON and a verified checksums.txt.

3) Patch SLAs & exception policy
- Critical (CVSS >= 9 or active exploit): 72-hour acknowledgement, mitigation or emergency patch within 30 days; hotfix windows available for dedicated customers with SLA addendum.
- High (CVSS 7-8.9): 7-day acknowledgement, remediation or mitigation within 90 days.
- Medium/Low: triaged per product release cycle (typically next sprint/quarter).
- Exceptions: formal exception requests documented in ticketing system, require CTO or Security lead signoff; emergency rollback policy exists for high-impact regressions.

4) SAST/DAST coverage
- SAST: internal AST pipeline using CodeScan Pro for pull-request gating on all services and nightly full-run; results retained for 24 months.
- DAST: authenticated DAST runs against staging on every sprint release; a comprehensive DAST + credentialed scan is scheduled quarterly. Findings are enriched with CVSS and exploitability notes in our vulnerability tracker.

Attached artifacts:
- redwood_vm_addendum_20270712.pdf (one-page answers + contact points)
- pen_test_summary_202706.pdf (redacted exec summary + CVSS table)
- sbom_snapshot_202706.zip (SPDX JSON + checksums)

If you need a fully unredacted pen-test package we can provide it under NDA and a short review window. Let us know what level the committee needs.

Next steps: we can deliver a scannable evidence bundle to your secure portal by Thursday; confirming scope and any PII redaction choices helps.

Best —
Rafael Mendes
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifications on pen test output, SBOM provenance, and patch SLAs

Rafael — quick note: the pen_test_summary is redacted for customer-facing distribution but includes full CVSS bins and mitigation status. For Everluma I'd recommend we remove any PoC exploit code and only include the CVSS and validation rows. Also confirm the SBOM ZIP does not contain any private keys — I saw checksums.txt is safe but double-check.

I can produce a version of the addendum that strips internal ticket IDs and developer comments; Priyom can produce the timeline table for remediation SLAs.

Marissa Cole
Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifications on pen test output, SBOM provenance, and patch SLAs

Marissa/Team —

I attached a remediation timeline table and proposed handoff dates to the shared drive (link in metadata). For Everluma:
- Emergency hotfix path (critical): patch candidate built and regression-tested within 14 days for dedicated customers; public-hosted customers: 30 days but with interim mitigations (WAF rules, feature toggles) within 72 hours.
- High: planned release within next two major releases (~45–90 days depending on backlog).

I'll also generate a short attestation that the SBOM export was generated from the build tag and that the composition scan ran with OSS-Guard v3.1.

Priyom Das
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood

From: Jordan Llewellyn <security@everluma.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@everluma.com, Michelle Tang <michelle.tang@everluma.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifications on pen test output, SBOM provenance, and patch SLAs

Rafael / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and level of detail. The redacted pen-test executive summary + SBOM snapshot meet our initial screening requirements. Procurement will accept the attestation in lieu of an unredacted report as long as we have an NDA executed for deeper review.

Next steps: procurement will issue a DocuSign for the standard master services agreement and the security addendum (I see the link in your cover note). Please expect an NDA request (we'll send the DocuSign today). Once NDA is fully executed, we'll request the unredacted pen-test artifacts for internal review.

Jordan Llewellyn
Head of Security, Everluma
